LPT: If your emergency brake light stays on even when it's released, you're low on brake fluid.
What about muffler bearings? Is there a light for those?
I just have my mechanic check it whenever I bring my car in to have the blinker fluid topped off.
Or you have a sticky float in the fluid reservoir.

Also your brake fluid being low could indicate worn brakes.

As your pads and discs wear down the pistons in your brake calipers have to travel further out, displacing fluid from the reservoir.

Most people just top it up as they see it going down so it defeats this purpose.
Or the E brake sensor is malfunctioning.
Aren't eBrakes mechanical? I know on all the cars I have had and did brake jobs on, the ebrake was a mechanical system and weren't tied into the hydraulics at all.
Its a parking brake, not an emergency brake.

Basically, he is saying that the warning light to tell you that the ebrake is on is the same light that comes on if you are low on fluid. If it comes on without the ebrake, it means low fluid. Normal times when you would see this is when you first start the car, release the parking brake and the light won't go off. Yes, most time the ebrake is mechanical (a wire) and the brake system is hydraulic. But the point is that the brake warning light is for both.
